name: Judeo-Iraqi Arabic

ancestors.notes: Judeo-Arabic macrolanguage node (ISO 639 jrb): a sociolinguistic/orthographic collective, not genetic descent (see jrb.json notes) -- yhd's single genetic PARENT is ar-IQ, matching the engine constraint that every language has at most one PARENT ancestor.

Regional descent: Judeo-Iraqi (Baghdadi Judeo-Arabic) is a qeltu-type Iraqi Arabic dialect, historically written in Hebrew script, distinct from the gilit dialect of Muslim Baghdad that ar-IQ.json describes.
Hebrew liturgical/lexical adstrate, shared with the rest of the Judeo-Arabic continuum (jrb.json).

notes: STUB. Judeo-Iraqi Arabic (ISO 639-3 yhd, confirmed this session via SIL/Ethnologue/Glottolog as denoting the variety spoken by Iraqi Jews, a member of the jrb macrolanguage), also called Baghdadi Judeo-Arabic. Like other qeltu (sedentary, pre-Hilalian-type) Mesopotamian Arabic dialects it preserves interdentals and the Classical Arabic /q/ where the Muslim Baghdadi 'gilit' dialect (ar-IQ.json) has innovated; it is historically written in Hebrew script rather than Arabic script. A complete letter-to-IPA grapheme table requires a dedicated phonological source (a JIPA illustration or descriptive grammar of Baghdadi Judeo-Arabic) that was not fetched with sufficient confidence this session; graphemes intentionally empty pending that sourcing pass. NOTE ar-IQ.json's own iso639_3 is 'acm' (the gilit/Muslim-Christian Mesopotamian Arabic macro-code); yhd is the separate code for the Jewish qeltu variety, hence the parent relation to ar-x-mashriqi's regional lineage via ar-IQ rather than identity with it.
